metadata.title: The logo-motion Skill
metadata.audience: Brutalist fellows already using Claude Code
metadata.note: Skill teardown of skills/make/logo-motion/SKILL.md. The logo-motion skill is ONE parametric Remotion composition (LogoMotion.tsx) that drives every logo sting — mark, wordmark, tagline, palette and LENGTH are all props, so a new brand is a traced part list plus a props block, never a copied scene. The scene enforces the emboss→materialise phase map measured off a reference sting (BUILD 0.03-0.16, GHOST HOLD 0.16-0.44, MATERIALISE 0.44-0.83, LOCK 0.83-1.00). This teardown covers: (1) the problem it stops — eight duplicated logo showcase files at 40-75KB each collapse into ONE composition; (2) the three-line integration — trace_logo.py emits runtime/remotion/src/logos/<name>.ts, one line in the LOGOS registry, one props block in the beat sheet; (3) MECHANISM ACT 1 — the build is a CAMERA move: staggering parts inward at ghost opacity is invisible, so the sting opens on an extreme close-up of the letterform and pulls back; (4) MECHANISM ACT 2 — the GHOST HOLD is the whole effect: 44% of runtime nearly invisible before one slow materialisation, verified against measured luma std-dev; (5) MECHANISM ACT 3 — LENGTH is a prop, not a re-time: durationInSeconds → durationInFrames, every ramp is a fraction of total; (6) MECHANISM ACT 4 — this skill is the AUDIO-FIRST EXCEPTION: the transition curve wins and narration waits for it, so runtime is transition + speech + tail; (7) FALSIFIABILITY — the three symptoms of a cheap sting: mark arrives at full strength (no ghost to arrive from), chrome/gloss sweep across a flat mark (stock template tell), colour arrives during motion (colour reads as part of the motion, not as an event). Renders in-toolkit against the shipped MEDHAVY_PARTS trace so the demo shows the actual phase map. Portrait companion is a native 9:16 build in vertical/ with SkillTeardown*916 wrappers registered in Root.tsx per feedback_hesitant_writer_portrait_scale and feedback_channel_title_portrait_bleed.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK-FIRST — anatomy of the logo-motion skill: SKILL.md doctrine, TIMING.md phase map, trace_logo.py, LogoMotion.tsx scene, LOGOS registry, per-brand parts.ts, reel's beat_sheet.json props.
beats.narration_text: First, the anatomy. On the skill side, SKILL dot md holds the doctrine and reference slash TIMING dot m d holds the phase map — measured off two real stings, not eyeballed. Alongside them, scripts slash trace underscore logo dot p y turns a raster mark into an animatable part list. The scene it drives is LogoMotion dot t s x — one composition, all props. It reads from a LOGOS registry — one line per brand — and each entry points at a per-brand parts dot t s file. The consumer is the reel's beat sheet — a props block that names the logo key and passes wordmark, tagline, palette, and length.

props.title: The logo-motion pieces.
props.calloutText: A new brand adds three things — never a fourth scene file. a per-brand parts.ts (via trace_logo.py), one line in the LOGOS registry, and one LogoMotion props block in the reel's beat sheet.

beats.role_note: The pipeline — four measured steps from a mark PNG to a rendered sting: TRACE PARTS, MEASURE LOCKUP, SET PHASE MAP, RENDER + LOOK.
beats.narration_text: The flow is four steps. Trace the mark into pieces — trace underscore logo dot p y crops to ink, upsamples four times, labels eight-connected components, and traces each one separately with potrace. Measure the lockup — take ink bounding boxes off a settled frame and put them into the scene as fractions, and position type by cap top, not by box top. Set the phase map — buildStart zero point zero three, ghost hold to zero point four four, materialise to zero point eight three. Then render and LOOK — pull a contact sheet. Never trust the probe. A ghost that is too short is invisible to ffprobe and obvious in a frame grid.

beats.role_note: Design decision 1 — the BUILD is a CAMERA move. Staggering parts inward at ghost opacity is invisible; opening extreme close-up and pulling back is what reads.
beats.narration_text: First design decision. The build is a camera move. The naive version staggers the traced parts inward on their own radial vectors, and calls that the geometric transition. At ghost opacity nobody can see it. The client's own words on the first cut of the Medhavy sting were, quote, it's just appearing. They were right. So the reference opens on an extreme close-up — the mark at six point five times scale, tilted nineteen degrees, filling and overflowing the frame — and pulls back to the settled lockup. Ease it hard. The big move is over early and the last third of the pull-back is a crawl. That is what makes it land, rather than stop.

body: extreme close-up · scale 6.5 · rotate -19° · easeOut hard
quote block lands verbatim from TIMING.md

props.heading: The build is a camera move.
props.body: Staggering parts inward on their own radial vectors is a geometric transition — but at ghost opacity it is invisible. The reference opens on an extreme close-up: the mark at ~6.5× scale, rotated -19°, offset, filling and overflowing the frame, then pulls back to the settled lockup. Ease it hard (1 − (1 − t)⁴): the big move is over early and the last third is a crawl, so it lands rather than stops. The camera IS the visible transition.
props.quote: It's just appearing. — the client's words on the first cut of the Medhavy sting.
props.cite: logo-motion reference/TIMING.md · The build must be a CAMERA move

beats.role_note: Design decision 2 — the GHOST HOLD is the whole effect: 44% of runtime nearly invisible, then one slow materialisation. Verified against measured luma std-dev.
beats.narration_text: Second decision. This is the whole architecture. The mark enters as a near-invisible emboss — pressed into the page, readable only as a shadow edge and a highlight edge — and stays that way for roughly the first half of the runtime. Then it materialises. One slow, continuous ramp from emboss to full ink. Measured in luma standard deviation across the reference sting, five percent contrast at p equals zero point three six, fifty percent at zero point six four, ninety-five percent at zero point eight zero. Forty-four percent of the runtime spent nearly invisible is not dead air being tolerated. It is the mechanism. The materialisation only reads as an arrival because there was nothing to arrive from.

show.event: eyebrow MECHANISM · ACT 2 lands
heading 'The ghost hold IS the effect.' fades in
body: BUILD 0.03-0.16 · GHOST 0.16-0.44 · MATERIALISE 0.44-0.83 · LOCK 0.83-1.00
quote block lands verbatim from TIMING.md
verdict pill '44% of the runtime, invisible'

props.heading: The ghost hold IS the effect.
props.body: Measured luma std-dev across the reference sting: 5% contrast at p=0.36, 50% at p=0.64, 95% at p=0.80. Phases (fractions of total): BUILD 0.03-0.16 (camera pull-back, parts converge underneath), GHOST HOLD 0.16-0.44 (settled, nearly invisible, floor sd≈2.6), MATERIALISE 0.44-0.83 (one slow smoothstep, emboss → full ink), LOCK 0.83-1.00 (static). Shorten the ghost and the arrival becomes a fade. There is nothing to arrive from.
props.quote: Half the runtime spent nearly invisible is not dead air being tolerated — it is the mechanism.
props.cite: logo-motion reference/TIMING.md · Why the ghost hold is the whole effect

beats.role_note: Design decision 3 — LENGTH is a PROP, not a re-time. durationInSeconds → durationInFrames via calculateMetadata; every ramp is a fraction of total; a 4s cut and a 9s cut are the same animation at different speeds.
beats.narration_text: Third decision. Length is a prop, not a re-time. durationInSeconds enters as a prop. calculateMetadata turns it into durationInFrames. Every ramp in the scene is a fraction of the total — buildStart zero point zero three, ghost zero point four four, materialise zero point eight three. So a four-second cut and a nine-second cut are literally the same animation, at different speeds. Never fork the scene to change length. Never eyeball a re-time. And this is deliberate — everywhere else in the toolkit duration falls out of measured narration. A sting is a fixed-length slot; a pre-roll is five seconds because the channel says five seconds. Length is INPUT here, and only here.

props.heading: Length is a prop.
props.body: durationInSeconds enters as a prop. Remotion's calculateMetadata derives durationInFrames from it. Every ramp in LogoMotion is a fraction of total — buildStart 0.03, ghost 0.44, materialise 0.83. A 4s cut and a 9s cut are the same animation at different speeds. Never fork the scene to change length; never eyeball a re-time.
props.quote: Length is a prop, not a re-time. A 4-second cut and a 9-second cut are the same animation at different speeds.

beats.role_note: Design decision 4 — the AUDIO-FIRST EXCEPTION. The transition curve wins and narration WAITS for it. Runtime is transition + speech + tail, an OUTPUT. Trim leading silence on any supplied track.
beats.narration_text: Fourth decision, and it is the exception that proves the toolkit rule. logo-motion is the one place in this toolkit where audio does NOT set the shape. Every other beat conforms to measured narration. Not this one. A sting reproduces a known motion. Re-timing the materialisation to land on a spoken word breaks the curve that makes it work. So the rule inverts. Run the transition to completion, then start the voice. Runtime becomes an output — transition, plus silence-trimmed narration, plus a short tail. If a supplied track carries leading silence, trim it before offsetting, or the voice starts late by exactly that much. On the Medhavy sting the leading silence was eight hundred and eighty milliseconds. That would have put the first word almost a full second inside a dead beat.

show.event: eyebrow MECHANISM · ACT 4 lands
heading 'The audio-first exception.' fades in
body: transition first, voice waits · runtime = transition + speech + tail · trim 0.88s leading silence
quote block lands verbatim from TIMING.md
verdict pill 'the curve wins, the voice waits'

props.heading: The audio-first exception.
props.body: Everywhere else in the toolkit, measured narration is the clock. Not here. A sting reproduces a known motion — bending the materialisation to land on a word breaks the curve that makes it work. Rule: run the transition to completion, then start the voice. Runtime is an OUTPUT — transition + (silence-trimmed) narration + tail. On the Medhavy sting, leading silence was 0.88s; delaying it by 7.00s would have put the first word at 7.88s, inside a dead beat.
props.quote: The transition wins, and the voice waits for it. This is the one place in the toolkit where audio does not set the shape.
props.cite: logo-motion reference/TIMING.md · When there is narration
props.verdictLabel: the curve wins, the voice waits

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY — the three symptoms of a cheap sting, ordered by frequency: (1) mark arrives at full strength — no ghost to arrive from; (2) chrome/gloss/bevel sweep — stock template tell, renders the mark's colour wrong during the pass; (3) colour arrives during motion — reads as decoration.
beats.narration_text: Falsifiability. When a sting looks cheap, TIMING dot m d gives you a diagnostic order. Check three things. Does the mark arrive at full strength? If yes, that is the bug. There is no ghost phase and nothing can materialise. Is there a chrome or gloss or bevel sweep? A hard-edged metallic gradient crossing a flat mark is the clearest tell of a stock template — and it renders the brand colour wrong for the whole time it passes. Does colour arrive during motion? Then it reads as part of the motion, rather than as an event. The Medhavy sting this skill was first used to fix had all three, at once. It popped the full lockup in two hundred and seventy milliseconds, held, then swept a silver gradient across a black mark — turning the brand mark grey for twenty percent of the runtime. Three tells, one wrong sting.

show.event: eyebrow FALSIFIABILITY · ACT 5 lands
heading 'Three tells of a cheap sting.' fades in
body: (1) full-strength arrival · (2) chrome/gloss sweep · (3) colour during motion
quote block lands verbatim from TIMING.md
verdict pill 'the Medhavy first cut had all three'

props.heading: Three tells of a cheap sting.
props.body: TIMING.md gives a diagnostic order for a sting that 'looks cheap': (1) Does the mark arrive at full strength? Then there is no ghost, and nothing can materialise. (2) Is there a chrome/gloss/bevel sweep? A metallic gradient across a flat mark is the stock-template tell — and it renders the brand colour WRONG while it passes. (3) Does colour arrive during motion? Then it reads as decoration, not as an event. The Medhavy first cut popped the lockup in 0.27s, held, then swept a silver gradient across a black mark from 2.80-4.00s — grey for 20% of the runtime.
props.quote: Check in this order: full-strength arrival, chrome sweep, colour during motion. All three were present in the first cut.
props.cite: logo-motion reference/TIMING.md · Diagnosing a sting that 'looks cheap'
props.verdictLabel: the Medhavy first cut had all three

beats.role_note: VERDICT — artifact card. Recapitulates the skill in six lines.
beats.narration_text: The verdict. logo-motion is one composition, every mark — the parts, the wordmark, the tagline, the palette, and the length are all props. The build is a camera move — extreme close-up, pull back, ease hard. The ghost hold is the whole effect — forty-four percent of the runtime nearly invisible, then one slow materialisation. Length is a prop, never a re-time — every ramp is a fraction of the total. It is the toolkit's audio-first exception — the transition curve wins, the voice waits. And a cheap sting fails in a fixed order — full-strength arrival, chrome sweep, colour during motion.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — Your Turn composer with a paste-ready measurement prompt. Liam reads aloud and discusses.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code. Read skills slash make slash logo-motion slash SKILL dot m d and reference slash TIMING dot m d. Take a logo sting you already have — any format Remotion can decode. Extract one frame per second with ffmpeg, and compute the luma standard deviation inside the mark's bounding box across the whole runtime. Find where contrast crosses five percent, fifty percent, and ninety-five percent, as fractions of total runtime. Compare those crossings against zero point three six, zero point six four, and zero point eight zero. If yours cross earlier, your ghost hold is too short. If they cross later, your materialisation is too slow. That is the measurement the skill was built to make cheap.

props.command: Read skills/make/logo-motion/SKILL.md and reference/TIMING.md. Take a logo sting I already have (any format Remotion can decode). Extract 1 fps with ffmpeg (`ffmpeg -i sting.mp4 -vf fps=1 _qc/frames/%03d.png`). Compute the luma std-dev inside the mark's bounding box for every frame; write it out as a CSV column. Find the p (fraction of total runtime) where std-dev crosses 5%, 50%, and 95% of the plateau. Report crossings vs. the reference (0.36 / 0.64 / 0.80). Do NOT modify the source sting; write CSV + plot into _qc/ only.
output: check: p_5 vs 0.36 — is my ghost hold long enough?
check: p_50 vs 0.64 — is my materialisation centred?
check: p_95 vs 0.80 — is my plateau on time?
